tasks.prompt: Warm-up: say 事 (si6, low flat tone 低平调) three times in a row. Low and flat, not mid like 試 si3, and not falling like 時 si4.
tasks.script: 事 si6 · 事 si6 · 事 si6 (compare: 試 si3 is mid-level; 時 si4 falls; 事 si6 sits lower and stays flat)

tasks.prompt: STAR #3 timed take (2 min, aim 260–280 words): say S-T-A-R aloud, then one follow-up: 'How did you deal with missing data?' Record, listen back once, fix one phrase. This is also warm-up for Mock A at 14:00. Watch: defensible (di-FEN-si-bul), governance (GUV-er-nunss), took the initiative TO.
tasks.script:
S: On an AI data-centre policy research programme, I was the sole analyst. The scope was ambiguous: there was no agreed definition of an 'AI data centre', the public data on energy, water, cooling, cost and land use was fragmented and inconsistent, and the project direction changed quite often.
T: My task was to build a defensible evidence base and policy analysis for urban and governance questions, even though the requirements were unclear and I had no one to review my work.
A: First, I pushed for a working definition of what counts as an AI data centre, so the whole analysis was built on the same scope. Second, I mapped the data gaps. I counted which indicators Hong Kong was missing and compared them with other governments and regions. Third, because the direction kept shifting, I built an iterative research workflow, so I could update the analysis step by step without starting again. And after every meeting, I kept a written log of what we agreed: the direction, the deliverables and the deadlines.
R: As a result, I delivered a baseline analysis of data-centre governance mechanisms from an international perspective, plus a clear list of the data Hong Kong is still missing, which gives future policy work a starting point.
Looking back: I learned that in ambiguous projects, confirming the scope early and keeping a written record protects both quality and timelines. Next time, I'd also structure the questions as an issue tree from day one.
Follow-up (missing data, ~30 s): I treated the gaps as a finding. I counted which indicators Hong Kong was missing, compared them with other regions, and the gap list became one of the deliverables.

tasks.prompt: Yue café + close: play both roles once. Ask for a seat, order something hot (no ice, less sugar), ask for a napkin, ask for the bill. Then say the 強項 line and the 時間/合作 closing. After that, in one breath explain why 事 / 試 / 時 sound different: point, reason, example.
tasks.script:
你: 唔該，有冇位呀？ · 店員: 有，呢邊。 (jau5, ni1 bin1)
你: 唔該，要熱嘅，走冰，少甜。 · 你: 唔該，要紙巾。 · 你: 埋單，唔該。
強項: 我嘅強項係數據分析同解決問題。
收尾: 多謝你嘅時間，希望有機會再合作。
Explanation: "事, 試 and 時 share the syllable si but not the tone. 事 is tone 6, low and flat; 試 is tone 3, mid and flat; 時 is tone 4 and falls. For example, 有咩事 uses the low one, 面試 uses the mid one, and 時間 uses the falling one."
